subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should this issue remain the umbrella for both high-frequency cron warnings and cron/session retention cleanup, or should maintainers split the remaining guardrails into narrower canonical issues now?
rationale: The code-backed gaps are real, but warning thresholds and base-session cleanup semantics affect operator behavior and persisted session state, so automation should not choose the product boundary alone.

options.title: Keep Umbrella Through Linked Slices
options.body: Use this issue to track the combined cron/session guardrail problem while maintainers review the retention PR and decide the warning behavior, then split only leftovers.

options.title: Split Remaining Guardrails
options.body: Create or confirm separate canonical issues for retention cleanup, high-frequency warnings, context-threshold warnings, and sessions cleanup behavior so each can close independently.

options.title: Narrow To Retention Only
options.body: If maintainers do not want a fixed frequency advisory, keep the source-backed retention bug path and close or reject the warning slice explicitly.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella Through Linked Slices
recommendation.body: Use this issue to track the combined cron/session guardrail problem while maintainers review the retention PR and decide the warning behavior, then split only leftovers.

likelyOwner.reason: The central unresolved choice is the cron/session lifecycle boundary introduced and maintained in the reaper path.
